transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Diego (CSM), Jared (BlueHarbor SRE), Priya (Head of ML), Marcus (Eng Mgr), Olivia (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): recurring 502s during surges; likely queue exhaustion + retry amplification; test plan agreed.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll try to keep this short. quick roll call?
[00:08] Jared: Jared here, sorry joining from SFO, we've got the log bundle up, saw a burst earlier around 11:40 PST with a lot of 502s.
[00:15] Priya: Priya here, high level: top priority is consistent p99 latency under spike for the content ingestion pipeline.
[00:22] Lina: Lina from Redwood, I'll take notes on the technical actions, also have the debug dashboard open.
[00:30] Marcus: Marcus, engineering manager, I'll own pilot criteria.
[00:36] Olivia: Olivia, product, just interested in timelines.
[00:40] Diego: Diego on CSM, making sure rollout happens smoothly.

[02:10] Samir: Quick recap of what we saw: during the mid-week campaign, BlueHarbor's prost-vm -- sorry, the Redwood endpoint returned a wave of 502s and we saw client-side retries pile up. We think a hotkey set caused a per-host queue to saturate and then the retry amplification made it worse.
[02:35] Jared: yeah, the logs show a few request IDs that match the same user session hitting the same shard, so some hotkeying for images. what do you mean by "per-host queue"?
[02:44] Lina: in our runtime there's a request-size limited queue per worker; if many long inputs land on the same worker, the queue grows and the worker starts rejecting. in logs that shows up as 502 on the frontend aggregator when the backend worker is overloaded. transcription sometimes shows "redwood dedi-cated" but it's Redwood Dedicated.
[03:01] Priya: got it. we do see that some jobs have 3x token length. can we avoid those hitting same worker?
[03:09] Lina: yes, two levers: adaptive routing to spread hotkeys, and KV cache warmup so repeated prefixes are served cheaper. also retry budget to avoid amplification.

[05:20] Marcus: What's the current retry policy? our client library by default retries 3 times with exponential backoff and jitter.
[05:28] Samir: Right now the SDK's client has a naive retry; on our side we recommend a retry budget plus an early circuit-breaker for 502/504s. Lina, remember the sample YAML?
[05:35] Lina: yes, I'll paste a sample after this call. high level: reduce client-side max retries to 1 for idempotent calls, add a server-side retry budget that caps retry tokens per user/session, and backoff with base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=25%.

[07:00] Jared: One confusing thing: sometimes it's 504 (gateway timeout) and sometimes 502. can you explain difference in terms of our stack?
[07:12] Lina: 504 usually means the front proxy waited for backend beyond its timeout; 502 is the backend rejecting because queue full or internal crash. both behave differently: 504 tends to be queue growth leading to timeouts; 502 often immediate rejection. we saw both patterns.

[09:50] Priya: The 5xx spikes were correlated with a marketing push that doubled qps for 10 minutes. We need a way to handle spikes without losing SLAs.
[10:02] Samir: Two approaches: smoothing at ingress (burst windowing / token bucket) and improving backend capacity (warm pools / prefetch). For the POC, we should prove that smoothing + retry budget reduces 5xx tails more than just adding capacity.

[12:15] Marcus: Are there known regressions with prefix caching when inputs are longer? We saw higher decode times.
[12:24] Lina: Longer sequences mean larger KV cache entries and longer per-token compute — caching helps when repeated prefixes exist; when sequences are unique caching doesn't buy you much. We can instrument prefix-hit rates.

[15:40] Samir: Quick demo of the dashboard — (audio glitches) — looks like the 99.9th percentile coincides with queue length crossing 80% of max. you can see spikes aligned with a handful of client IPs.
[16:02] Jared: yep, that's the hotkey group. can we shard those users differently?
[16:10] Lina: we can add a routing rule to hash on a different key (user id mod N) rather than session token; that'll spread load, but will change cache locality. tradeoff: fewer hotkeys per worker but more cache misses.

[18:50] Priya: what's the expected impact on latency if we change hashing?
[18:56] Lina: median might increase slightly (5-10ms) due to more cache misses, but p99 should drop because no worker gets crushed. worth it for you?
[19:10] Marcus: yes p99 is the primary metric. throughput can be tuned later.

[21:22] Jared: About the retry budget experiment — how do we validate it?
[21:27] Samir: plan: 1) baseline run with current client retries during a controlled spike, 2) run with client retries reduced and server-side retry budget enabled, 3) run with smoothing at ingress. Compare p99/p999 and error rate.
[21:42] Lina: we'll add probes that inject x-req-id header so we can track amplification (original request vs retried counts).

[24:10] Olivia: timeline please, when can you provide the YAML?
[24:14] Lina: by 2027-01-06, sample config + canary ramp steps.

[25:00] Samir: Jared, can you run the controlled spike? We'll provide the script.
[25:05] Jared: yes, target is 1.5x baseline qps for 10 minutes; we can run it on 2027-01-07 morning.

[27:30] Priya: One more oddity: some requests show very high backend processing time without being long inputs; maybe contention on GPU?
[27:42] Lina: Could be KV eviction or kernel stall; we'll ask Redwood infra to check per-GPU utilization. also request IDs will show if same worker handled many concurrent long jobs.

[29:55] Marcus: any quick mitigation we can enable that doesn't require code change?
[30:00] Samir: server-side: turn on soft limit on per-worker inflight and return 429 rather than 502 when queue is near full. client-side: switch to 1 retry. both are config flips.

[32:10] Jared: prefer returning 429 as it's kinder to orchestrators, they can queue and back off. 502 triggers client confusion.
[32:18] Lina: agree - we'll suggest min-change config that maps backend rejections to 429 for now.

[34:40] Priya: any privacy/compliance concerns with adding x-req-id?
[34:46] Diego: x-req-id is just an opaque id; no PII. but we'll note it in the security doc.

[36:00] Samir: Competitor note — we talked briefly about Vertex's autoscale; their approach is vertical scale per endpoint which reduces p99 only if kernels are optimal. For you, sharding + retry budget is lower risk.

[38:20] Lina: I'm going to outline the YAML: sample retry-bucket: tokens-per-minute=1000, per-user-cap=5, per-session-cap=2, token-refill=60s. circuit-breaker: trip when worker rejection > 5% for 30s. backoff base 200ms.

[40:10] Marcus: For canary, can we route 5% of traffic through this policy for 1 hour, check key metrics, then 20%?
[40:17] Lina: yes, that's the recommended ramp. also add a fallback model variant with smaller memory (quicker) to keep latency bounded.

[42:05] Jared: We'll need the fallback model artifact — is that a Redwood-managed variant?
[42:12] Samir: We can provide a compatible quantized variant (Redwood-compact-1) for the pilot. it's slower on quality but much more predictable.

[44:30] Priya: Quality tradeoff acceptable for edge cases where SLA trumps fidelity.

[46:00] Olivia: recap of decisions?
[46:05] Samir: 1) collect logs with x-req-id, 2) run control spike 2027-01-07, 3) Redwood to propose retry-budget + map 502->429 soft reject, 4) canary ramp plan, 5) consider routing change if needed.

[47:20] Marcus: we'll also define pass/fail: p99 < 300ms and error rate < 0.5% during spike window.

[48:50] Jared: one more question: if the retry budget reduces retries, won't client experience more errors?
[48:58] Lina: short-term yes but overall error amplification will decrease; clients should surface graceful fallback. Also with smoothing + fallback variant we keep user-visible errors low.

[50:15] Samir: ok I'll send a thread with the requested artifacts: dashboard export, annotated logs, and the sample YAML. Lina will attach the retry policy.
[50:26] Diego: I'll set the follow-up meeting for next Wednesday, 2027-01-13.

[51:10] Samir: thanks everyone, appreciate the actionability here.
[51:15] Priya: thanks, happy new year.

(Transcription notes: occasional speaker attribution errors, some product names mis-transcribed like "Redwood dedi-cated" or "retrial" instead of retry budget; timestamps are approximate.)
